blockers.title: APScheduler fires N times per cron tick with multi-worker uvicorn
blockers.description: The module-level `workflow_scheduler = WorkflowSchedulerService()` is a per-process singleton. The Helm deployment (helm/charts/backend/values.yaml) runs uvicorn with 4 workers. Each worker runs the lifespan, calls `workflow_scheduler.start(db)`, and registers all schedules independently. When a cron expression fires, all 4 workers independently execute `_trigger_scheduled_run`, creating 4 duplicate workflow runs per scheduled trigger. Requires either restricting to a single worker process, an external distributed job store (e.g. APScheduler with SQLAlchemy jobstore + row-level locking), or moving scheduling out of the app process entirely.

blockers.title: list_excursions return value not unpacked in search query branch
blockers.description: Before this diff the query branch read `items, total_items = await excursion_service.list_excursions(...)`, correctly unpacking the (list, count) tuple. The refactor changed it to `items = await excursion_service.list_excursions(...)` without unpacking. Since list_excursions returns tuple[list[dict], int | None], `items` is now the full tuple instead of the list. The else-branch correctly handles this with `items_and_count[0]`, but the if-query branch skips that step, causing a malformed API response for any search request.

suggestions.title: workflow_type path param not validated against schedule's actual workflow type
suggestions.description: GET/PATCH/DELETE /{workflow_type}/schedules/{schedule_id} fetch the schedule by ID and check org membership, but never verify schedule.workflow_type_definition_id matches the workflow_type in the URL. A user can request GET /workflows/other-type/schedules/{id} for any org-member schedule and receive 200 with workflow_type='other-type' in the response body, which is factually wrong.

suggestions.title: last_run_at recorded as successful even when workflow trigger fails
suggestions.description: In _trigger_scheduled_run the DB update setting last_run_at=now is placed after the try/except block. The except clause swallows the exception and logs it, then execution falls through to the unconditional update. If create_workflow_run raises (e.g. Prefect unreachable), last_run_at is still written, making failed triggers indistinguishable from successful ones in the UI.

suggestions.title: No rate limiting on schedule CRUD endpoints
suggestions.description: POST/PATCH/DELETE schedule endpoints do not call check_rate_limit() unlike other workflow endpoints. An authenticated user can create an unbounded number of schedules (e.g. * * * * * every-minute jobs), with no per-org ceiling, creating an effective DoS against the workflow execution system.

suggestions.title: list and create silently use orgs[0] for multi-org users
suggestions.description: Both list_workflow_schedules and create_workflow_schedule use orgs[0] to determine org_id rather than accepting an explicit org context. A user in multiple orgs always creates/lists schedules under whichever org the repository returns first, which is inconsistent with GET/PATCH/DELETE that correctly check the full org set.

suggestions.title: _trigger_scheduled_run does not revalidate creator's org membership
suggestions.description: When a schedule fires it calls create_workflow_run with created_by=schedule.created_by and org_id=schedule.org_id taken directly from the stored row. If the original creator has since been removed from the organization, the run still executes under their user ID indefinitely, allowing a deprovisioned user to continue triggering privileged runs via schedules created before deprovisioning.

suggestions.title: update_schedule unconditionally overwrites next_run_at on every PATCH
suggestions.description: update_schedule always recomputes next_run_at from datetime.now() even when only name or is_enabled changed. A schedule due in 5 minutes shows a different next_run_at after a rename. Fix: only recompute when cron_expression or timezone is in updates.

suggestions.title: No input length constraints on schedule name, cron_expression, or timezone
suggestions.description: CreateScheduleRequest and UpdateScheduleRequest declare unbounded str fields. Other string fields in the codebase use Field(max_length=...) or Query(le=...). Very large strings increase attack surface against croniter and DB payload size.

suggestions.title: APScheduler job missing coalesce=True; restart storm possible
suggestions.description: misfire_grace_time=300 means a 5-minute downtime replays all missed ticks for all enabled schedules simultaneously on restart. Adding coalesce=True would collapse multiple missed fires into a single catch-up execution per schedule.

blockers.title: list_excursions tuple not unpacked in search path — response body corrupted
blockers.description: list_excursions() returns tuple[list[dict], int|None]. In the 'if query:' branch the result is assigned directly to 'items' without unpacking: `items = await excursion_service.list_excursions(...)`. The filters dict already contains 'search': query (set at line 92), so list_excursions enters its search branch and returns (items_list, total_count). The raw tuple then flows into `"items": items` in the response, serialising as a 2-element JSON array [items_list, count] instead of the list of excursion objects. Any frontend call with a query string will receive malformed pagination data. Fix: unpack the tuple — `items, _ = await excursion_service.list_excursions(...)`.

suggestions.title: total_items count ignores extra_workflow_run_ids expansion in search path
suggestions.description: count_filters does not include 'extra_workflow_run_ids', so the count_excursions call returns the total for the base workflow_run_id only. But the items list is widened by extra_run_ids from resolve_search_workflow_run_ids. The displayed total_items may therefore undercount the true number of matching excursions when the search resolves additional run IDs. Consider adding the resolved run IDs to count_filters or documenting the intentional mismatch.

suggestions.title: last_run_at updated even when create_workflow_run raises
suggestions.description: In _trigger_scheduled_run, the update block that sets last_run_at and next_run_at runs unconditionally after the try/except around create_workflow_run. A failed run will still mark the schedule as 'last run at now', which can mislead operators into thinking the run succeeded. Consider tracking success/failure separately or only updating last_run_at on success.

suggestions.title: Two cron engines compute next_run_at — slight time mismatch possible
suggestions.description: _compute_next_run uses the 'croniter' library while APScheduler uses its own CronTrigger internally. The two engines may disagree by up to one second on the next-fire time, causing the next_run_at stored in the DB to differ from when the job actually fires. For display purposes this is harmless, but it could confuse monitoring tooling that compares the DB value to actual fire times.

suggestions.title: No way to clear 'parameters' to null via PATCH endpoint
suggestions.description: update_workflow_schedule uses model_dump(exclude_none=True), so a client sending {"parameters": null} in JSON results in 400 ('No fields provided to update') rather than clearing the parameters field. If callers ever need to remove parameters from a schedule, this is not possible through the current API. Document the limitation or use a sentinel pattern to distinguish 'not provided' from 'explicitly null'.
